key: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted for his mother.
s: Closing the servant’s errand, Isaac meets the returning caravan at evening; Rashi, on 24:67, reads it as Rebekah becoming like Sarah, the lamp burning from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, the blessing in the dough and the cloud over the tent returning with her.

evidence.words: וַיְבִיאֶהָ הָאֹהֱלָה וְנַעֲשֵׂית דֻּגְמַת שָׂרָה אִמּוֹ, כְּלוֹמַר וַהֲרֵי הִיא שָׂרָה אִמּוֹ, שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁשָּׂרָה קַיֶּמֶת הָיָה נֵר דָּלוּק מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וּבְרָכָה מְצוּיָה בָּעִסָּה וְעָנָן קָשׁוּר עַל הָאֹהֶל, וּמִשֶּׁמֵּתָה פָּסְקוּ, וּכְשֶׁבָּאת רִבְקָה חָזְרוּ
evidence.gloss: He brought her into the tent and she became the likeness of Sarah his mother, that is, behold, she is Sarah his mother; for all the while Sarah lived a lamp burned from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, blessing was found in the dough and a cloud was bound over the tent; when she died they ceased, and when Rebekah came they returned.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 24:67, at [23,67]). Opened the packet for 24:67: Rashi’s comment headed האהלה שרה אמו says Rebekah became like Sarah and that the lamp from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, the blessing in the dough and the cloud over the tent, which ceased at Sarah’s death, returned when Rebekah came; the sentence paraphrases exactly that and adds nothing (Rashi cites Genesis Rabbah, but the comment is his and is cited as his). Plain sense faithful: the servant’s errand ends here, and Isaac meets the camels at eventide in 24:63. Evidence recopied from the packet character for character. Entry unchanged; entry-check ok.
